q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a rotavator?
title: Rotavator carbon footprint per unit
short: A rotavator is mostly steel: weigh the sheet, plate, blades and gearbox parts per unit and multiply by your suppliers' per-kg figures. Add cutting, welding, machining and painting energy, then divide the plant's energy by units built.
audience: Farm implement makers in Punjab and Rajkot

ul: Steel sheet and plate for the frame and cover.
Boron steel blades and the gearbox castings.
Laser or plasma cutting and press bending.
Paint shop: pretreatment, powder or liquid paint and oven.

p: Report per rotavator by working width, since a 7 foot model carries much more steel than a 4 foot one.

example.title: Worked example: rotavator unit per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 25,770 / 150 = 171.8 kg CO2 per unit
Add steel, castings and blades for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
